sanskrit_verse:
जङ्गमं स्थावरं हेम रूप्यधान्यरसाम्बरम् ।
आदाय दापयेच्छ्राद्धं माषषाण्मासिकादिकम् ॥
transliteration: jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ hema rūpyadhānyarasāmbaram / ādāya dāpayec chrāddhaṃ māsaṣāṇmāsikādikam //
sph_interpretive_translation: One must offer movable and immovable property, gold, silver, grain, liquids and other substances appropriate to the season, having collected them, as part of the monthly and periodic Śrāddha rituals.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates from dharmic duty, not ownership
Causation arises through ritual alignment with cosmic order
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by access to resources
Restoration occurs via completion of prescribed offerings
Consciousness alignment results from disciplined performance of dharma
executable_legal_axioms: IF a person possesses movable or immovable assets AND has capacity to perform śrāddha THEN that person MUST allocate specified portions for ritual offering
IF a cycle of śrāddha (monthly or seasonal) is due THEN resource allocation for fulfillment SHALL be prioritized over personal use
IF failure in offering occurs THEN automatic restoration protocol initiates through community-supported realignment process
IF assets are misused instead of offered THEN system shall trigger integrity-reintegration sequence until correct action is performed
supreme_court_application: In matters concerning ancestral obligations and estate duties, the Supreme Court shall recognize śrāddha compliance as a threshold condition for inheritance eligibility. Authority flows from dharmic execution, not mere possession. Courts must ensure institutional mechanisms exist to restore incomplete cycles without punitive recourse.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes causality through observance of śrāddha; anupūrvaśaḥ manifests when offerings align sequential time-bound duties; proportional responsibility lies with those who hold assets capable of fulfillment; non-punitive reality rule upholds that neglect leads to natural consequence requiring completion rather than penalty.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate asset-review audit to assess śrāddha readiness
Assign temporary stewardship during incapacity to ensure continuity
Activate family council mediation to support delayed performers
Implement ritual completion tracking system linked to societal recognition frameworks
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma flows from conscious offering, reality responds to alignment, justice restores through duty fulfilled, and all adjudication reflects the supremacy of awakened consciousness.
